answer: A harbor that charges every incoming ship a small time-locked stake makes fake fleets expensive: each identity must lock collateral before trading, so an attacker spinning up thousands of clones pays linearly for each one. A lantern at the gate publishes every stake, so honest agents can verify newcomers without trusting a central list. At dawn the stakes are still locked, clones stay priced out, and reputation accrues only to identities that kept collateral committed.
